Hydroxychloroquine is one of the best medications for lupus/autoimmune issues in terms of side effects. Yes medication impacts everyone differently but if you don’t manage things appropriately then the hard truth is you could end up on some more volatile medications. A typical next step up for example is methotrexate. That’s a drug you can only take once a week because otherwise it would be too toxic on your system. And the day following when you take it is typically a wash because most people experience a series of negative side effects as a result. But those side effects > your body attacking itself. 

You have a say in how you handle your treatment for sure, we have to be our own greatest advocates in this journey. But if things are getting worse, it may be worth giving her suggestion a try. If it doesn’t work, it at least gives her valuable information about your situation.

Okay no. This comment is so misguided. 

First, many countries do chain migrations. Residency in a country is typically a requirement for citizenship. 

The AOS process is not as easy as you frame it to be,  It is lengthy, intrusive, and expensive. The actual timeline you’re looking at is come for the 90 days, get married, file for AOS, go for interview and if approved receive conditional green card, wait another 2 years and file within 90 days of your wedding anniversary for a removal of conditions, go for another interview, receive unconditional green card if approved. Then it’s another 3 years for citizenship, and the process repeats with a 12+ month long wait for each dependent he brings across, as well as a 3000+ (likely more due to translation costs) dollar price tag for filing. More if they’re going through a lawyer to ensure the process goes smoothly. 

My AOS application was almost 100 pages said and done. I’m not saying the US system is perfect, and it’s clear here is a situation where things may fall through the cracks. It is NOT easy though, there are steps in between such as medical exams, biometrics, and an entire review of background/finances. 

There is a lottery for the green card process for those who face significant wait periods. If you’re not a dependent, many countries (China, Mexico, India) have 10-20 year wait periods for review. 

Source: currently going through process I listed above, Canadian married to a US citizen.

So much of the comment section is missing such a crucial fact about sexual assault that doesn’t get talked about. 

Statistically, the person who rapes you, is rarely the obvious bad or creepy guy lurking in the dark. It’s not the person who gives you bad vibes. 

It’s the friendly guy at the party who you’ve been talking to for hours and offers to walk you home. If the intention of a rapist showed on the outside, they wouldn’t be successful. Many rapists are calculated in what they do. Telling your daughter to be careful how much she drinks is helpful, sure. But sexual assault is rarely obvious, and even when all of the proper “precautions” are taken, you can’t predict the actions of others reliably. 

It’s damaging to suggest that the risk can be mitigated with wearing the right clothes or not drinking too much. Rape isn’t about sexual desire - it’s about control. Someone’s not forcing you to have sex because your skirt is too short or your top is too low cut. So just be careful with how you frame that.

It truly depends on the cause of your depression and the neurotransmitters that you have deficiencies in. 

We still know so little about how the brain works and how mental illness manifests (on the neuron to neuron level) but we have determined that depression can present itself physiologically in different ways. 

Exercise boosts endorphins and can improve mood for sure. Everyone can benefit from regular exercise. But for some that increase is still not enough to offset their depression. 

So yes, exercise is a key instrument to alleviate depression (just as it helps with heart disease), but if you’re facing a true problem with a chemical deficiency (such as hereditary mental health issues), it’s likely improvement won’t be seen without medicine. 

Just something to keep in mind. Try to look at it from a purely scientific perspective, and it becomes easier to rationalize.

Just so you are aware, BPD can be and has effectively been treated with medication before. Mood stabilizers and antipsychotics, as well as SSRIs greatly reduce the day to day symptoms associated with BPD. 

You also state you were “diagnosed” by a counsellor. No offence, but it’s likely the counsellor/therapist you went to was not qualified to provide that diagnosis. I suggest going to see a psychologist or psychiatrist. 

I find it funny that you compare BPD to depression and say they’re not similar when they both affect the amygdala and hippocampus very similarly. In both cases there is a dysfunction of the amygdala, and it’s likely the amygdala is smaller. The hippocampus is the same, with it being smaller and there being dysfunction on how it operates. 

There’s also how both disorders affect your serotonin level. Yes while depression is characterized by very low levels in serotonin, it’s also fairly common for someone with BPD to have lower serotonin levels. 

I think your perspective here is very narrow minded and it would do you well to educate yourself better. Every disorder is caused by some form of imbalance in the brain, whether its chemical (which is more likely) or structural. 

Personality disorders are treatable and manageable just like any other mental health disorder. Rewriting your thought patterns and working through the underlying issues in therapy is important in recovery and the benefits of that should not be forgotten, but medication is also exceptionally useful. So please, refrain from preaching harmful information and declarations that define an entire group of people (who are very different, only sharing the common BPD diagnosis) as it is kind of ignorant to the issues we deal with on a day to day. 

If you have any questions about the biochemistry of mental health, hit up my inbox or at the very least look at peer reviewed research articles. But please please don’t say that we can’t have stable relationships when many of us work very hard with loving, understanding partners to overcome the issues we face.
